A_trait: floral morphology; nectar traits; robbed versus unrobbed flower state across distylous morphs
decision_note: Primary Tirpitzia study measures floral traits, robbery susceptibility, hawkmoth visitation and reproductive fitness. Floral morphology predicts robbery, but matching pollinator response to the same morphological axes is not isolated, so retain as near-pass rather than H1 trait geometry.

A_trait: robbed versus unrobbed floral state / nectar access
decision_note: Primary Sesamum study compares pollinator behaviour and seed set on naturally robbed versus unrobbed flowers. Xylocopa latipes acts both as primary robber and legitimate pollinator; role is consumer-state dependent.

A_trait: floral colour morph and manually robbed versus unrobbed tree state
decision_note: Primary Tecomella experiment manually increases nectar robbery and shows changed pollinator foraging plus increased fruit set. Robbery state is the manipulation; the floral colour morphs do not provide a matched opposing trait-response geometry.

A_trait: flowering patch context along elevation; robbed-flower frequency
decision_note: Primary Clinopodium study quantifies legitimate visitor communities, nectar robbery and seed production along a 1000-m elevational gradient. It is strong spatial interaction-context evidence but not a same-trait H1 geometry study.
